name: Pondi
confidence_why: Barlow (2020), the only description of Pondi and the work of its sole fieldworker, states that stress is not phonemic and that disyllables take penultimate or final stress with only a slight penultimate preference, and no other source has described the language.
catalog_citation: Barlow, Russell. 2020. A Sketch Grammar of Pondi. Canberra: ANU Press (Asia-Pacific Linguistics). Chapter 2, Phonetics and phonology.
catalog_quote: 2.4 Stress Stress in Pondi is not phonemic. In single-word utterances, disyllabic words may receive stress either on the ultima or on the penult, although there is perhaps a slight preference for penultimate (trochaic) stress. In longer words and phrases, pragmatic factors play a significant role in stress assignment, although there is nevertheless a tendency for stress to fall on alternating syllables. There is no phonemic tone, nor are there other suprasegmental phonemic distinctions found in the language.

audit.reasoning: The record rests on the only existing description of Pondi, a 2020 ANU Press sketch grammar by the language's sole fieldworker, held in full; the deciding passage is confirmed verbatim at sect. 2.4 p. 35. The classification 'variable' (non-phonemic stress, disyllables penult-or-final with slight trochaic preference, longer words pragmatically driven with alternating tendency, no fixed position) is a faithful reading of that paragraph. nothing to add to the list of works to obtain.
